4.label: Exceeds Standard
4.description: Demonstrates deep understanding; solves complex, multi-step problems accurately; explains reasoning clearly.

3.label: Meets Standard
3.description: Consistently applies grade-level concepts correctly with minor errors; meets all CCSS expectations.

2.label: Approaching Standard
2.description: Partially applies concepts; makes procedural errors; inconsistent accuracy across question types.

1.label: Below Standard
1.description: Limited or no grasp of grade-level concepts; significant errors; unable to complete standard tasks independently.

standards.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (e.g., 35 = 5 × 7).

levels.4: Correctly interprets and writes multiplicative comparison equations; explains both directions of the relationship.
levels.3: Correctly interprets multiplicative comparisons and writes matching equations with no more than 1 minor error.
levels.2: Partially interprets comparisons; confuses additive vs. multiplicative; inconsistent.
levels.1: Cannot interpret or write multiplicative comparison equations correctly.

standards.description: Solve multiplicative comparison word problems using multiplication and division.

levels.4: Solves multi-step comparison problems; shows clear equation setup and labels; no errors.
levels.3: Solves single-step comparison word problems correctly; may make minor computational errors.
levels.2: Sets up problem partially correctly; frequent computational or conceptual errors.
levels.1: Unable to set up or solve comparison word problems.

standards.description: Solve multi-step word problems using the four operations; assess reasonableness using estimation.

levels.4: Solves complex multi-step problems; uses estimation to verify; explains strategy.
levels.3: Solves most multi-step problems correctly; uses estimation at least once to check reasonableness.
levels.2: Solves single-step parts but struggles with multi-step sequencing; limited estimation use.
levels.1: Cannot solve multi-step problems; no evidence of estimation strategy.

standards.description: Find factor pairs, determine whether a number is prime or composite (1–100).

levels.4: Lists all factor pairs for any number 1–100; correctly classifies prime/composite; explains why 1 is neither.
levels.3: Finds most factor pairs; correctly identifies prime vs. composite numbers with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Finds some factors but misses pairs; makes errors classifying prime/composite.
levels.1: Cannot identify factor pairs or distinguish prime from composite.

standards.description: Generate and analyze a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule.

levels.4: Generates correct pattern; identifies multiple features not explicitly stated in the rule; explains with precision.
levels.3: Generates a correct pattern from a rule; identifies one non-obvious feature.
levels.2: Generates partially correct pattern; does not identify additional features.
levels.1: Cannot generate or analyze a pattern from a given rule.

standards.description: Recognize that a digit in one place represents ten times the digit to the right.

levels.4: Explains and applies the 10× relationship across multiple place values; connects to multiplication.
levels.3: Correctly identifies the 10× place value relationship in all standard examples.
levels.2: Understands the concept for tens/hundreds but inconsistent for larger place values.
levels.1: Cannot describe the relationship between place values.

standards.description: Read, write, and compare multi-digit whole numbers; use comparison symbols.

levels.4: Reads, writes (standard, word, expanded form), and orders multiple large numbers with full accuracy.
levels.3: Correctly reads, writes, and compares multi-digit numbers using <, >, = with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Reads and writes numbers but makes errors in comparison or expanded form.
levels.1: Significant errors reading, writing, or comparing multi-digit numbers.

standards.description: Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place using place value understanding.

levels.4: Rounds accurately to any place; explains decision process; applies rounding in context.
levels.3: Rounds to any specified place correctly with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Rounds to tens/hundreds correctly but struggles with larger places.
levels.1: Cannot reliably round to any place value.

standards.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

levels.4: Applies standard algorithm fluently; zero errors; can identify and correct others' errors.
levels.3: Correctly solves multi-digit addition/subtraction with ≤1 computational error.
levels.2: Uses algorithm but makes regrouping errors in ≥2 problems.
levels.1: Does not use or apply the standard algorithm correctly.

standards.description: Multiply a whole number up to four digits by a one-digit number, and two two-digit numbers.

levels.4: Solves all multiplication types accurately; shows work; uses multiple strategies (area model, algorithm).
levels.3: Correctly multiplies 4-digit × 1-digit and 2-digit × 2-digit with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Correct for smaller numbers; makes errors with larger or two two-digit multiplications.
levels.1: Cannot reliably multiply multi-digit numbers.

standards.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors.

levels.4: Correctly divides with remainders; interprets remainder in context; uses multiple strategies.
levels.3: Correctly finds quotient and remainder for most problems with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Finds quotient but makes errors with remainders or larger dividends.
levels.1: Cannot perform multi-digit division or consistently find correct quotients.

standards.description: Explain why a/b = (n×a)/(n×b); recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

levels.4: Generates multiple equivalent fractions; explains the multiplication/division reasoning; applies to simplification.
levels.3: Correctly generates equivalent fractions and explains the n×a/n×b relationship.
levels.2: Generates some equivalent fractions by procedure but cannot explain why they are equal.
levels.1: Cannot identify or generate equivalent fractions.

standards.description: Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators using <, >, =; justify using benchmarks.

levels.4: Compares fractions using multiple strategies (common denominator, benchmarks, cross-multiply); explains choice.
levels.3: Correctly compares fractions and provides valid justification with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Compares correctly when denominators are related; struggles with unrelated denominators.
levels.1: Cannot reliably compare fractions with unlike denominators.

standards.description: Understand addition/subtraction of fractions as joining/separating parts of the same whole; add/subtract mixed numbers.

levels.4: Adds and subtracts mixed numbers with regrouping; decomposes in multiple ways; no errors.
levels.3: Correctly adds and subtracts fractions and simple mixed numbers with like denominators.
levels.2: Adds/subtracts simple fractions correctly; errors when regrouping mixed numbers.
levels.1: Cannot add or subtract fractions correctly.

standards.description: Apply understanding of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

levels.4: Solves fraction × whole number problems in multiple contexts; writes as repeated addition and as product.
levels.3: Correctly multiplies a fraction by a whole number; connects to repeated addition.
levels.2: Multiplies simple cases correctly but errors with larger whole numbers or mixed results.
levels.1: Cannot multiply a fraction by a whole number.

standards.description: Express fractions with denominators 10 or 100; add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.

levels.4: Converts fluently between tenths and hundredths; adds correctly; connects to decimal notation.
levels.3: Correctly expresses and adds fractions with denominators 10 and 100 with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Adds when denominators match; struggles converting tenths to hundredths.
levels.1: Cannot work with tenths/hundredths fractions.

standards.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

levels.4: Converts fluently in both directions; places decimals on number line; explains place value connection.
levels.3: Correctly reads and writes decimals to hundredths; matches to equivalent fractions.
levels.2: Writes tenths as decimals correctly; errors with hundredths or fraction-decimal matching.
levels.1: Cannot convert between fraction and decimal notation.

standards.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths using <, >, =; justify using place value.

levels.4: Compares decimals accurately; explains place value reasoning; places decimals on number line.
levels.3: Correctly compares decimals to hundredths with valid place value justification.
levels.2: Compares decimals with same number of decimal places; errors with mixed tenths/hundredths.
levels.1: Cannot reliably compare decimals.

standards.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within a system; convert larger to smaller units.

levels.4: Converts within and across multiple unit systems; applies in multi-step problems.
levels.3: Correctly converts larger units to smaller units (e.g., km→m, hr→min) with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Converts simple, frequently practiced pairs; errors on less familiar conversions.
levels.1: Cannot reliably convert between measurement units.

standards.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, time, volume, and money.

levels.4: Solves complex multi-step measurement word problems; labels units; checks reasonableness.
levels.3: Correctly sets up and solves measurement word problems with ≤1 computational error.
levels.2: Solves single-step measurement problems; struggles when unit conversion is embedded.
levels.1: Cannot set up or solve measurement word problems.

standards.description: Apply area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and mathematical problems.

levels.4: Applies formulas correctly; works backwards from area/perimeter to find missing dimensions; no errors.
levels.3: Correctly calculates area and perimeter using formulas with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Confuses area and perimeter; applies one formula correctly but not both.
levels.1: Cannot apply area or perimeter formulas correctly.

standards.description: Make a line plot to display fractional data; solve problems involving information in the line plot.

levels.4: Creates accurate line plot with labeled axes; solves addition/subtraction problems from plot.
levels.3: Creates correct line plot and answers questions about the data with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Creates line plot with minor errors; answers basic reading questions but not analysis.
levels.1: Cannot create or correctly interpret a line plot with fractional data.

standards.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes; measure angles with a protractor in whole-number degrees.

levels.4: Measures all angles accurately (±2°); classifies correctly; draws angles to specification.
levels.3: Measures most angles correctly with ≤5° error; correctly classifies acute/right/obtuse/straight.
levels.2: Measures common angles (90°, 180°) correctly; inconsistent with non-standard angles.
levels.1: Cannot use protractor correctly or classify angles reliably.

standards.description: Recognize angle measure as additive; find unknown angles using addition/subtraction.

levels.4: Solves multi-step unknown angle problems; writes and solves equations; explains reasoning.
levels.3: Correctly finds unknown angles using additive reasoning in standard configurations.
levels.2: Finds unknown angles when one decomposition is given; struggles with two-step problems.
levels.1: Cannot apply additive angle reasoning to find unknown angles.

standards.description: Draw and identify points, lines, line segments, rays, and angles (right, acute, obtuse).

levels.4: Accurately draws and labels all geometric figures; identifies in complex diagrams without prompt.
levels.3: Correctly draws and labels all required figures with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Identifies most figures when labeled; struggles to draw from description.
levels.1: Cannot reliably draw or identify basic geometric figures.

standards.description: Classify 2D figures based on parallel/perpendicular lines and angle types.

levels.4: Accurately classifies all 2D figures; explains hierarchy (e.g., square is a rectangle); uses correct terminology.
levels.3: Correctly classifies 2D shapes by lines and angles with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Classifies common shapes (square, rectangle); errors with less familiar shapes or overlapping categories.
levels.1: Cannot classify 2D shapes using parallel/perpendicular criteria.

standards.description: Recognize and draw lines of symmetry for 2D figures.

levels.4: Identifies all lines of symmetry for any figure; draws them correctly; explains why asymmetric figures have none.
levels.3: Correctly identifies and draws lines of symmetry for standard shapes with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Identifies obvious symmetry (vertical axis); misses diagonal or multiple lines of symmetry.
levels.1: Cannot reliably identify or draw lines of symmetry.
